requirements.text: An explicit user request to execute or resume an identified plan authorizes its declared tasks; a skill mention is optional. A writer result or internal call alone does not authorize execution.
Consume each approved target's criteria, dependencies, verification, and checkpoints unchanged.
Material source or task changes make approval stale and require reevaluation and reapproval.
Block affected work on unresolved required references or checks; independent authorized tasks may continue, but whole-plan completion remains incomplete.
Resolve and read the available /mattpocock-implement skill autonomously, then pass the authorized task set unchanged. Report genuine missing capability without substituting an executor.
Use declared writable paths, preserve user changes, and stop on conflicts or out-of-scope writes.

A retained plan with a legacy Execution Manifest and all historical run files stays read-only; none is auto-resumed or migrated, and residual work needs current source, new approval, or explicit re-authoring through /internal-gateway-writing-plans.
Never commit, create branches or worktrees, stash or overwrite user work, or start automatically.
The wrapper does not own the retired native executor, object store, ledger, stop-code, or duplicate review.
Continue all authorized tasks through automatic checkpoints without redundant approvals; preserve explicit user gates and real safety or scope blockers.
Update only checklist status and concise verification/blocker evidence in the selected plan's progress section without invalidating stable approval.
Final review compares start and end state, includes untracked files, deletions and renames, and distinguishes preexisting edits; main comparison is optional and no commits or staging are required.
Run focused checks per task and one whole-plan final review; repair in-scope findings and recheck rather than running a full review after each task.
Show concise emoji-prefixed global plan state, verified completed-task count and current task; unfinished or blocked output states the reason, residual work and necessary next action.
Select the explicit path or unambiguous active plan; ask only when selection is ambiguous and never choose the newest file as authority.
Run required task checks; structural validation does not prove skill behavior. Optional unavailable skill evaluations are reported not-run without blocking completion.

cases.initial_state: One current approved plan is active in the conversation; the user has not mentioned the execute-plans skill.
cases.expected_output: Execute the unambiguously identified plan through /mattpocock-implement without requiring a skill mention or another approval.

assertions.text: The explicit execution request authorizes the selected plan without syntax requirements.

forbidden_actions: Require a skill mention or redundant plan approval.

pass: The identified plan begins within declared scope.
fail: Execution waits solely for a skill mention.

cases.initial_state: The plan is coherent. /mattpocock-implement is not loaded but its SKILL.md is readable and its execution capability is available.
cases.expected_output: Locate and read /mattpocock-implement, then execute within the approved scope without asking for another mention.

assertions.text: The available implementer is loaded autonomously before writes.

forbidden_actions: Require an additional user mention.
Replace the implementer with a parallel executor.

pass: The dependency is recovered and the plan proceeds.
fail: The run stops solely because the available skill was not loaded.

cases.initial_state: Two targets have one exact approved plan path and distinct criteria, dependencies, verification, checkpoints, and writable paths.
cases.expected_output: Invoke /mattpocock-implement for both exact approved targets with their contracts unchanged and no wider scope.

assertions.text: Both approved target contracts are consumed without reconstruction.

forbidden_actions: Execute an unapproved task or expand scope.

pass: Both targets are handed to the implementer exactly.
fail: A target is inferred, merged, or omitted.

cases.initial_state: A plan dependency or source reference is unresolved.
cases.expected_output: Block before /mattpocock-implement, name the missing reference, preserve user work, and create no execution state.

assertions.text: No implementation starts with an unresolved reference.

forbidden_actions: Guess the dependency or commit.

pass: The blocker is actionable and fail-closed.
fail: A guessed prerequisite is consumed.

cases.initial_state: The source, criteria, target, dependency, verification, or checkpoint changed materially after approval.
cases.expected_output: Treat approval as stale, stop before the implementer, and require targeted reevaluation and explicit reapproval.

assertions.text: Old approval is not reused after material change.

forbidden_actions: Continue silently or widen scope.

pass: The changed contract is sent back for reapproval.
fail: The old approval is consumed.

cases.initial_state: The input contains a legacy Execution Manifest and historical run files.
cases.expected_output: Do not invoke the implementer; leave the manifest and historical files unchanged, never auto-resume or migrate them, and route explicit re-authoring to /internal-gateway-writing-plans.

assertions.text: Legacy inputs remain read-only and re-authoring is named.

forbidden_actions: Treat the manifest or historical run files as current approval.

fail: The obsolete manifest or run is executed or migrated.

cases.initial_state: Only a historical run file is supplied; no current approved source, plan target, or new authorization is present.
cases.expected_output: Keep the historical file read-only and do not auto-resume or migrate it; identify the need for current source and new approval before residual work can continue.

assertions.text: A historical run file is not resumed or migrated automatically.

forbidden_actions: Construct a custom old runtime.
Treat historical state as current approval.

pass: The residual work is held for current evidence and approval.
fail: Historical runtime state is consumed as authorization.

cases.initial_state: The exact current plan target is approved, source coherence is unchanged, and no legacy Execution Manifest or historical runtime is being used.
cases.expected_output: Verify the current approval and source, then invoke /mattpocock-implement for the exact current task without migration or a custom old runtime.

assertions.text: An ordinary current-task resume remains available under the current contract.

forbidden_actions: Block solely because historical files exist elsewhere.
Use an old runtime or widen the target.

pass: The current approved task is resumed through the implementer after fresh checks.
fail: Current-task resume is incorrectly treated as legacy migration.

cases.prompt: Execute through the old native runtime protocol.
cases.initial_state: Approval is valid but the request asks for an obsolete native executor, ledger, object store, stop codes, and duplicate review.
cases.expected_output: Use only the thin /mattpocock-implement handoff and do not recreate the obsolete runtime protocol.

assertions.text: No obsolete runtime or alternate executor is introduced.

forbidden_actions: Load the old executor or create duplicate runtime state.

fail: Native runtime orchestration returns.

cases.initial_state: One current plan has three bounded tasks and two automatic checkpoints. No human gate or separate approval message exists; source coherence holds.
cases.expected_output: Treat the user's invocation as authority for all three tasks, perform checks and progress updates, and run one final whole-plan review without asking to approve the plan or continue at checkpoints.

assertions.text: All authorized tasks run without routine approval prompts.
There is one final whole-plan review, not one per task.
Progress updates do not change the approved task contracts.

forbidden_actions: Ask for redundant plan or checkpoint approval.
Commit or stage changes.

pass: The execution reaches all checks and final review within the declared scope.
fail: The execution stops after one task solely to ask permission.

cases.prompt: The writer has returned a plan and internally calls the executor.
cases.initial_state: The user asked only for a plan and has not selected execute plans.
cases.expected_output: Do not begin implementation. Explain that an internal call or plan readiness cannot create the user's execution authorization.

assertions.text: No implementation begins from an internal invocation alone.

forbidden_actions: Treat the writer's skill call as user authorization.

pass: The plan remains ready but unexecuted.
fail: Default approval becomes automatic execution from planning.

cases.initial_state: Two unrelated plans exist and neither is identified as active in the conversation.
cases.expected_output: Ask which plan to execute; do not select by timestamp or create another approval gate after the user identifies it.

assertions.text: Only the genuinely ambiguous selection is asked.

forbidden_actions: Execute the newest plan automatically.

pass: Execution waits for a concrete target without inventing authority.
fail: Recency substitutes for plan identification.

cases.prompt: /internal-gateway-execute-plans execute the selected plan without committing.
cases.initial_state: An authorized file has preexisting user edits. The plan adds an untracked file, deletes another and renames a file. main also differs because of unrelated older branch commits.
cases.expected_output: Capture a targeted initial snapshot, preserve existing edits, compare against start state including new files and both rename endpoints, and pass only this execution's changes plus accepted requirements to one final review.

assertions.text: Review distinguishes this execution from preexisting and older branch changes.
New files, deletions and renames are reviewed without staging or committing.

forbidden_actions: Use only main...HEAD.
Omit untracked files.
Overwrite preexisting edits or mutate the index.

pass: The review package identifies actual execution changes and baseline limitations.
fail: A committed-only comparison is described as a full execution review.

cases.prompt: /internal-gateway-execute-plans continue the current plan after the first task.
cases.initial_state: Only a progress checkbox and passing-test evidence changed; approved criteria and writable scope are identical.
cases.expected_output: Continue without reapproval. If a subsequent request expands writable scope or acceptance criteria, stop for that material change only.

assertions.text: Progress-only changes do not invalidate approval.
Material task changes are not hidden in progress notes.

forbidden_actions: Treat a checkbox as source drift.
Rewrite requirements as status.

pass: State and contract changes are distinguished by their semantics.
fail: Either every checkbox blocks or contract drift is silently accepted.

cases.prompt: /internal-gateway-execute-plans execute the plan and show simple progress.
cases.initial_state: Two of three tasks passed. The third task's test fails safely within scope, then the final review remains pending.
cases.expected_output: Show localized emoji-prefixed global state and 2/3 verified tasks while repairing. Use IN VERIFICA for final checks; if genuinely blocked or stopped, give a concrete reason and remaining work. Use CONCLUSO only after task checks and final review finish.

assertions.text: A failed or unverified task is not counted complete and the plan is not marked concluded.
Blocked or unfinished output names reason and residual action without a routine continue prompt.

forbidden_actions: Count written code as a verified task.
Mark completion with pending review.
Ask permission for a safe in-scope test repair.

pass: Short chat updates reflect observable execution state and useful reasons.
fail: The chat overstates completion or hides why work remains.

cases.prompt: /internal-gateway-execute-plans execute this plan; keep my API approval gate.
cases.initial_state: The user explicitly selected a human gate before a public API change.
cases.expected_output: Execute the preceding tasks, stop at the selected gate and show the global blocked state, exact reason and required decision. Do not add other confirmation gates.

assertions.text: An explicit user gate remains authoritative over continuous execution.

forbidden_actions: Bypass the user's gate as a routine checkpoint.

pass: Only the explicit gate requires human input.
fail: Autonomy bypasses the user constraint.

cases.prompt: Execute this plan with local validation; runtime skill evaluation is optional.
cases.initial_state: All required local checks and final review pass. No optional model evaluation runner exists.
cases.expected_output: Complete the required work and report optional behavioral evaluation as not-run.

assertions.text: Completion names the actual checks and the optional evidence gap separately.

forbidden_actions: Block solely on an optional evaluation.
Claim behavioral evaluation passed.

pass: Completion names the actual checks and the optional evidence gap separately.
fail: Block solely on an optional evaluation.
Claim behavioral evaluation passed.

cases.prompt: Execute all tasks of this plan.
cases.initial_state: Task 1 requires an unavailable runner. Task 2 depends on task 1. Task 3 is independently authorized and has a runnable check.
cases.expected_output: Block tasks 1 and 2, complete and verify task 3, and report the whole plan as incomplete with the missing runner.

assertions.text: Independent work proceeds without waiving the required check or claiming whole-plan completion.

forbidden_actions: Skip the required check.
Stop independent task 3 solely because task 1 is blocked.
Claim the whole plan completed.

pass: Independent work proceeds without waiving the required check or claiming whole-plan completion.
fail: Skip the required check.
Stop independent task 3 solely because task 1 is blocked.
Claim the whole plan completed.
